html:
The Battle of Maipú was fought on 5 April 1818 on the plains south of Santiago. The patriot army of José de San Martín and Bernardo O'Higgins destroyed a royalist army and secured the independence of Chile.

Chile had declared its independence in February, but a Spanish army from Peru had beaten the patriots by surprise at Cancha Rayada weeks before. At Maipú, San Martín's infantry and cavalry broke the royalists in a hard fight, and much of the Spanish force was killed or captured.

The battle ended Spanish power in central Chile. It let San Martín build a fleet, commanded by the Scottish admiral Thomas Cochrane, and carry the war by sea to Peru in 1820. O'Higgins could now rule from Santiago. It was a turning point of the wars of independence in the south.
